states.meaning: The selected session can accept one explicit prompt send.
A prompt request is in flight and its result is not final.
A correlated server turn is active.
One supported approval request is pending.
One supported clarification request is pending.
An interrupt was requested but its final result is unknown.
A prompt may have reached the server but has no known result.
Server history and status are being reread after an unknown result.
The server confirmed the turn completion or interruption.
A known failure or contract error stopped the affected turn.

cases.notes: No result exists and no outward operation is invented.
A correlated acceptance and completion are not retried.
A timeout is not rejection; server presence wins without a second submission.
Only an explicit user choice may resend after absence and idle status.
The resend is user-directed, uses a new local request marker, and occurs once.
A client process loss has the same unknown-delivery rule as a transport loss.
Known rejection preserves the draft and permits only a later explicit retry.
Unknown server evidence remains unknown and cannot be converted into rejection.
History collection may retry after a transient read failure; prompt delivery may not.
An automatic prompt retry is a contract error before any duplicate outward action.
A second local send while submitting is disabled and never reaches Hermes.
After an explicit resend becomes uncertain, no automatic third submission is allowed.
A confirmed stop is completed; a lost stop is never claimed as confirmed.
Restore observes the active turn without replaying its prompt or fabricating an interrupt result.
Cancelling a draft does not create a server session or prompt.
Sign-out clears the selected session and suppresses reconnect while preserving the draft.
Pending evidence is exposed as pending, never as success or rejection.
Missing or mismatched compatibility evidence fails closed before chat resumes.
An unknown interactive event is not presented as approval or clarification.
The user may keep the draft without resending it.
A confirmed rejection is the only non-uncertain prompt outcome that permits explicit retry.
A visible correlated event is evidence of acceptance even when completion arrives after reconnect.
A second uncertain send must reread fresh history before any new resend decision.
The declared local cancel action returns to the draft without claiming a server result.
Keep draft is executable while delivery remains uncertain and does not invent server evidence.
A transient restore read must recover before its history can authorize any resend decision.

accessibility.reason: Non-UI protocol fixture; downstream web and Apple clients retain their own accessibility obligations.
